info.title: Power Platform API
info.description:
The Power Platform API is Microsoft's documented control plane for Power Platform administration, organised into namespaces — environment management, licensing, governance, connectivity, app management, Power Pages, Copilot Studio, analytics and more.

Requests carry an `api-version` query parameter. Alongside the global host, some operations are addressed on **tenant-scoped** (`{tenantId}.tenant.api.powerplatform.com`) or **environment-scoped** (`{environmentId}.environment.api.powerplatform.com`) hosts, where the host itself identifies the scope and the path carries no id.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered — see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/ppapi) for how it was derived and which parts are verified.

servers.description: Global endpoint. Every documented operation is reachable here; the gateway routes the request to the tenant's own cluster. First-party clients use it for operations that are not already scoped to one tenant or environment by the caller's context.

Tenant-scoped endpoint. The host is derived from the tenant id alone — there is no region or scale-unit in it. Remove the hyphens from the tenant id to get 32 hex characters, then split: the first 30 are the first DNS label and the remaining 2 are the second. Tenant `00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ab` therefore resolves to `https://000000000000000000000000000000.ab.tenant.api.powerplatform.com`. Operations served only here act on the calling user or the tenant as a whole and take no tenant id in the path.

tenantIdHead.description: The first 30 characters of the tenant id with its hyphens removed.

tenantIdTail.description: The last 2 characters of the tenant id with its hyphens removed.

servers.description: Environment-scoped endpoint. Built from the environment id by the same rule as the tenant host: strip the hyphens to get 32 hex characters, take the first 30 as the first DNS label and the last 2 as the second. Environment `00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ab` resolves to `https://000000000000000000000000000000.ab.environment.api.powerplatform.com`. The environment is implied by the host, so these paths carry no `/environments/{environmentId}` segment — `/connectivity/connections` here is the same resource as `/connectivity/environments/{environmentId}/connections` on the global host.

environmentIdHead.description: The first 30 characters of the environment id with its hyphens removed.

environmentIdTail.description: The last 2 characters of the environment id with its hyphens removed.

tags.name: Advisor Chat
tags.description: A conversational assistant that answers questions about the tenant in prose, backed by whatever the service knows about it. Separate from the advisor recommendations in the same namespace, which return structured findings against specific resources, and from the solution-checker advisor on another host entirely. Preview: the surface is feature-gated in the only client known to call it.

tags.name: Cluster
tags.description: The regional service cluster that serves a tenant or an environment. Its name appears in the `x-ms-gateway-clusters` response header on every call and identifies which stamp, geography and release ring the caller is talking to.

tags.name: Copilot Governance Setting
tags.description: A single tenant- or environment-level consent switch for a generative AI capability — typically whether a named model provider may be used as a subprocessor. Each setting carries its own admin-centre presentation, the rule that backs it and the effective value.

tags.name: Environment
tags.description: Create; Delete; Disaster recovery configuration; Link Dataverse; Managed governance; Management settings; Read model

tags.name: Environment Operations

tags.name: Feature Gate
tags.description: A named feature flag as evaluated for the caller or the environment. Read-only: the platform decides the value and reports where it came from.

tags.name: Governance Configuration
tags.description: Tenant-authored governance content surfaced to makers in the maker portal, addressed by configuration name.

tags.name: Notification
tags.description: In-product notifications for the calling maker, and the Web PubSub channel that pushes them live.

tags.name: Service Plan
tags.description: The Power Platform service plans (licences) assigned to the calling user, and the policy limits each plan grants.

tags.description: A per-user preference blob stored against the caller's Entra object id and addressed by setting name. The maker portal uses them to persist UI state; each setting name has its own free-form shape.

get.description:
Lists the advisor conversations belonging to the calling user. The caller is taken from the token, so there is no way to list another user's threads here. Each entry gives the id to pass as `conversationId` when resuming a thread.

> **From Microsoft's own client, not observed live**
>
> - Found in the pac CLI's `advisor` module (pac CLI 2.11.2), which is gated behind the `ModuleAdvisor` feature flag and absent from the CLI's own published command manifest. It is also absent from Microsoft.PowerPlatform.Management, the generated client that covers the rest of this namespace — so the released internal OpenAPI does not describe it yet. Treat it as preview surface that can change or disappear.

post.description:
Asks the Power Platform advisor a question about the tenant and returns its answer. Omit `conversationId` to start a new conversation; the response carries the id the service assigned, and passing it back on the next request continues the same thread with its history intact. Answers are generated, so they take seconds to minutes rather than milliseconds — pac allows five minutes before giving up, and a client should budget similarly rather than using a default HTTP timeout.

This is not the solution-checker advisor at `advisor.powerapps.com`, and it is unrelated to the advisor recommendations elsewhere in this namespace: those return structured findings about resources, this returns prose.
